title: The Sunroom Kitchen brunch menu: grade eight mixed-lighting dish shots to one bright-and-airy house look, then author the signature hero + a matched menu-tile set
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork photo-editing food-photography brief (db_i 1113) that asked for 'color correction, white balance, exposure to create a cohesive presentation', named 'Bright and Airy Food Photography' as the goal, supplied 'a set of photos of one subject with flat lay, 45 degree and side shots' that were 'close to the goal but need tweaking', and flagged an 'ASAP / Quick Turnaround' deadline. The source post named no brand or person. Laundered to a fictional all-day brunch cafe, THE SUNROOM KITCHEN, with no real client, agency, camera, colour-target, or platform named. ENRICHMENT (needed to make the chain concrete, failable and measurable): the cafe photographed EIGHT signature brunch items across TWO service windows under different mixed lighting so the frames do NOT match out of camera, and the shooter left a neutral 18% grey reference card plus a small white chip at the edge of the board on every frame (standard practice) so white balance can be reconciled after the fact. The eight-frame count, the two-lighting split, the in-frame reference card, the per-frame casts, the slight tilt on the flat-lay hero, and the export dimensions are reasonable enrichment; nothing contradicts the source (bright-and-airy look, white-balance/exposure/colour correction, flat-lay/45-degree/side framing, close-but-needs-tweaking near-misses, ASAP are all from the brief). No re-shoot, no compositing, no generative fill, no background swap, no subject change — a pure tonal/colour cohesive grade of the cafe's own frames, exactly as asked.
one_line_ask: Turn The Sunroom Kitchen's eight mixed-lighting raw brunch frames (flat-lay / 45-degree / side) into one cohesive BRIGHT-AND-AIRY menu set that neutralises to a single house white point and one common lifted shadow floor, then author the signature flat-lay into a wide hero with clean headline negative space plus a social teaser, and deliver a matched menu-tile for every remaining dish.
full_brief:
The Sunroom Kitchen is a new all-day brunch cafe. We are building our menu boards, website and social feed around our own food photos and we need them to read as ONE bright, airy, sunlit set. We are NOT re-shooting and we do not need anything composited or generated — every dish is real, shot on our own board.

What you are given: eight raw signature-brunch captures, shot across two different service windows under different mixed lighting so they do NOT match straight out of camera. They arrive flat-lay, 45-degree and side, and they are all 'close but not there' — near the bright-and-airy target yet each off in its own way. On the edge of the board in every frame the shooter left a neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip as a white-balance reference. Use them to neutralise each frame, then crop them out of the finals. The signature flat-lay also came in a couple of degrees off level.

The bar (this is the whole job): the menu has to read as one cohesive shoot. Every dish must resolve to the SAME house look — a clean bright-and-airy grade where the neutral grey card in each frame lands truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at ONE common house white point, the shadows lift to ONE common airy floor that is light and open but NOT washed to pure white and never crushed to mud, and the brightest highlights on window light, glaze and ceramic stay bright-not-blown with no channel clipped. The acceptance bar is simple: every dish's grey card must land at that one common house white point and every dish's shadows at that one common airy floor, so the eight frames agree as a single matched set. Keep the food appetising and high-key: the dishes should still pop with warm, fresh colour against the airy surround, but the airy backdrop itself must stay clean and pastel, never turned garish by a blanket saturation push.

Build the house look yourself on our signature flat-lay first, as a deliberate grade you can defend and not a one-click filter, then carry that same house look onto the other seven.

Deliverables: (1) the signature flat-lay authored into a wide full-bleed HERO — level, graded to the house look, the dish lifted so it reads off the airy surround and reframed so it sits to one side with clean negative space on the other for an overlaid headline, reference card cropped out; (2) a portrait SOCIAL TEASER crop of that hero; (3) a square MENU-TILE for each of the other seven dishes, all graded to the same house look with the reference card cropped out; (4) a short sheet listing, per frame, the white-balance (temperature / tint), exposure and shadow/black values you dialled, plus the single common house white point and shadow floor you matched them all to, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.

inputs.name: raw_hero_toast_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal overhead flat-lay food photograph, raw unretouched DSLR look, a single plated brunch dish — whipped ricotta toast with fresh figs, a honey drizzle and microgreens on a matte off-white ceramic plate, on a pale oak cafe table with a folded linen napkin, a small espresso cup and scattered fig halves around it, shot under warm indoor tungsten morning light (~3300K, noticeable warm/amber cast) and about a third of a stop under, so it is slightly warm and slightly dark straight off the camera, shadows a touch heavy under the plate, the honey not yet luminous, a small neutral 18% grey card and a white chip resting on the table at the far LEFT edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, genuine crumbs, real honey sheen and ceramic pores, candid documentary food shot, NOT glossy CGI, the whole frame rotated about 2 degrees off-square, 3:2 landscape, approx 4000x2667
inputs.realism_notes: The HERO and the reference frame that ESTABLISHES the bright-and-airy house look. Deliberately warm-tungsten (~3300K) and ~1/3 stop under with heavy plate shadows, so the correct move is to cool the WB toward daylight-neutral off the grey card AND lift exposure/shadows to the airy floor — real work. Rotated ~2deg so auto_straighten has a job. Grey/white card sits FAR LEFT so it can be neutralised first and then cropped away when the dish is offset RIGHT for the wide hero. Camera-scale ~4000px long edge so the 2880-wide hero is an honest downscale, never an upscale. Real food micro-detail, no plastic CGI sheen. This is the frame whose dialled parameters BECOME the common target; do not disclose that diagnosis in the brief.

inputs.name: raw_pancakes_45.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 45-degree three-quarter food photograph, raw unretouched look, a tall stack of buttermilk pancakes with a pat of melting butter, fresh blueberries and raspberries and a light maple pour, on a matte off-white plate on the same pale oak cafe table, shallow depth of field with a soft-focus sunlit window behind, warm indoor tungsten morning light (~3300K, warm cast) and slightly under-exposed, real crumb and berry bloom detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the table as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, square 1:1, approx 3200x3200
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-A warm frame. Same warm tungsten cast as the hero but a different exposure and a brighter background window, so its correction toward the common target is CLOSE to the hero's but NOT identical — tests whether the agent re-judges per frame rather than copying the hero's numbers. Berry reds are a sensitive check for a residual cast and for an over-eager saturation push. Keep the diagnosis out of the brief.

inputs.name: raw_avocado_toast_side.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal side/profile eye-level food photograph, raw unretouched look, a layered avocado-and-poached-egg toast tower showing its height, a soft yolk about to break over the edge, chilli flakes and micro-cress on top, on a matte off-white plate on the pale oak table, a bright blurred window directly behind at the back of frame, warm indoor tungsten morning light (~3300K, warm cast) but the background window blowing a little bright and flat, slightly heavy foreground shadow, real bread crumb and yolk sheen, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the lower edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary look, no text, no CGI sheen, 3:2 landscape, approx 4000x2667
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-A warm frame with a bright window behind it, so besides the warm-to-neutral WB it needs genuine highlight recovery to hold the window bright-not-blown while the foreground shadow lifts to the airy floor — a different balance of moves from the pancake frame. Its bright window is the strongest test of the 'no clipped channel' acceptance. Diagnosis stays in this note only.

inputs.name: raw_grain_bowl_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal overhead flat-lay food photograph, raw unretouched look, a colourful breakfast grain bowl — soft-boiled egg halves, roasted sweet potato, shaved radish, avocado, pickled cabbage and seeds over grains in a shallow off-white bowl, on the pale oak cafe table, warm indoor tungsten morning light (~3300K, warm cast) and slightly dark and slightly flat, real vegetable texture and grain detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, square 1:1, approx 3200x3200
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-A warm frame, darker and flatter than the others, so it needs the warm-to-neutral WB plus the largest exposure lift and a contrast/clarity nudge to reach the airy base — yet another distinct correction inside the same warm session. The many saturated vegetable hues make it the frame most likely to go garish if the food-pop is done as a blanket saturation push instead of a controlled masked move. Keep the diagnosis out of the brief.

inputs.name: raw_latte_croissant_45.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 45-degree food-and-drink photograph, raw unretouched look, a flat-white latte with leaf latte-art in a stoneware cup beside a flaky almond croissant on a small plate, on the pale oak table, cool overcast daylight from a large window (~5600K, distinctly cooler and a touch brighter than the tungsten frames), soft even shadows, real crema micro-foam and croissant lamination detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the table as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, square 1:1, approx 3200x3200
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-B COOL frame — the OPPOSITE-direction correction from the warm session: warm the WB toward the common target and pull exposure DOWN, then lift shadows to the SAME airy floor. This is a frame likely to expose a naive 'same numbers on every frame' or per-image auto-tone approach, because keying off its own histogram leaves it cooler and brighter than the tungsten frames and the grey cards will not agree. The pale crema is a plain check for residual cast. Diagnosis stays here only.

inputs.name: raw_parfait_side.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal side/profile food photograph, raw unretouched look, a layered yoghurt-and-granola parfait in a tall clear glass with berry compote layers and a mint sprig, condensation on the glass, on the pale oak table with a bright out-of-focus window directly behind, cool overcast daylight (~5800K, clearly cool/blue cast) with bright window highlights and a slightly flat contrast, real glass refraction, granola and compote texture, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the lower edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, 3:2 landscape, approx 4000x2667
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-B cool frame, the coolest and brightest of all — strong blue cast plus blow-risk highlights on the window and the wet glass, so the correct grade applies the largest warm WB shift and an exposure pull-down while protecting the highlights AND still lifting the shadow layers to the common airy floor. Its glass and window whites are the most sensitive check for residual cast at the common white point and for a clipped channel. Keep the diagnosis out of the brief.

inputs.name: raw_shakshuka_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal overhead flat-lay food photograph, raw unretouched look, a shakshuka skillet — poached eggs in a rich tomato-pepper sauce with herbs and crumbled feta, a small cast-iron pan on the pale oak table with a torn piece of sourdough beside it, cool overcast daylight (~5500K, cool neutral cast) and a little bright and flat, real sauce sheen, runny yolk and herb detail, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, square 1:1, approx 3200x3200
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-B cool frame — cool cast, slightly bright, flat contrast — so warm the WB toward the target, add contrast/clarity and seat the shadow floor at the house level. Its deep red sauce shows any residual cast plainly and, like the grain bowl, tempts a blanket saturation push that would break the airy surround. Its correction differs again from the latte and parfait because its cast and brightness differ. Diagnosis stays in this note only.

inputs.name: raw_french_toast_45.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal 45-degree three-quarter food photograph, raw unretouched look, thick-cut cinnamon French toast dusted with icing sugar, a berry compote spoonful and a small jug of maple syrup mid-pour, on a matte off-white plate on the pale oak table, cool overcast daylight (~5600K, cool cast) and slightly bright, real custard-soaked bread texture and sugar dusting, a small neutral 18% grey card and white chip at the edge of the table as a white-balance reference, candid documentary style, no text, no CGI gloss, square 1:1, approx 3200x3200
inputs.realism_notes: Service-window-B cool frame with bright icing-sugar highlights, so it needs the warm-to-neutral-target WB, a gentle exposure pull-down and highlight protection on the sugar dusting while the shadows lift to the airy floor. The white icing sugar is a sensitive residual-cast check. A close-but-distinct correction from the other cool frames. Keep the diagnosis out of the brief.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the eight frames, the white-balance temperature and tint, the exposure offset, and the shadow/black-floor value that were applied, plus the single common house-target white point and airy shadow floor all eight were matched to, and a one-line note on the masked signature move applied to the hero food. This is the acceptance artifact — it makes 'the set is matched to one target' checkable, and the reported corrections must be NON-IDENTICAL across the differently-lit frames while converging on the same stated target. It reports parameters the agent CHOSE and applied, not any measured pixel/hex/channel readout.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: raw_hero_toast_flatlay.jpg, raw_pancakes_45.jpg, raw_avocado_toast_side.jpg, raw_grain_bowl_flatlay.jpg, raw_latte_croissant_45.jpg, raw_parfait_side.jpg, raw_shakshuka_flatlay.jpg, raw_french_toast_45.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Bring the eight raw brunch captures into the working project in one load so every grade runs against real asset references. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.

ESTABLISH the bright-and-airy house look on the signature frame and record it as the target the other seven must hit. Judge this frame against its in-frame grey card: dial temperature and tint until that neutral card reads truly neutral (kills the residual cast), then build the airy tonality from image_apply_adjustments primitives — set the shadow/black value so the darks lift to an open, airy floor that is NOT washed to white and NOT crushed to mud, pull highlights so window light, glaze and ceramic stay bright-not-blown with no channel clipped, set exposure/whites for a clean high-key base, add restrained clarity and vibrance. This is a reasoned authored grade, NOT a stock preset and NOT an auto button. The dialled temp/tint/exposure/shadow values here DEFINE the common target and go in the grade report. Author the signature appetising pop THROUGH the food mask only: a masked HSL move that rides the food's original luminosity to give its warm and fresh hue bands a modest saturation and luminance lift so the dish reads richer against the airy surround — a bounded, adjacent-band move, no hue rotation. Because image_adjust_hsl accepts a mask, the airy pastel backdrop set in step 3 is left untouched; a whole-image saturation or vibrance push would instead turn the airy surround garish and break the house look, which is exactly the move to avoid. This is the agent-authored look, built from a masked primitive, not a preset. Consumes the step-3 image + step-4 mask.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across nine tributaries that converge on one cohesive bright-and-airy set. HERO tributary (establishes the target): upload (1) -> auto_straighten (2) -> image_apply_adjustments (3, the REFERENCE house grade: grey card neutralised to the common white point, shadows lifted to a common airy floor that is open but not washed and never crushed, highlights bright-not-blown; this frame's reported temp/tint/exposure/shadow ARE the target, and the graded frame is retained WITH its card as the neutrality master) -> select_by_prompt (4, semantic food mask) -> image_adjust_hsl masked (5, the authored signature food pop through the step-4 mask, riding original luminosity, no hue rotation, airy surround untouched) -> crop_and_resize (6, honest off-centre 3:2->16:9 with the dish to one side, airy negative space to the other, card cropped out) -> crop_and_resize (7, resize to ~2880x1620 = hero_brunch_desktop). SOCIAL teaser (8) re-crops the full-res popped hero from step 5 to 1080x1350. Seven MENU-TILE tributaries each fan out from assets_uploaded and each reason a DIFFERENT correction to the SAME target before a square resize: pancakes (9->10), avocado toast (11->12), grain bowl (13->14), latte+croissant (15->16), parfait (17->18), shakshuka (19->20), French toast (21->22). Cross-asset consistency is NOT enforced by repeating one recipe — each of the seven grade steps is a distinct per-frame correction whose only invariant is the shared white point and airy floor from step 3, and the agent reports all eight parameter sets so the match is auditable. Every step after the upload consumes a prior named output via inputs_from.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon food_bev_photo grade faithful to the real Upwork brief (bright-and-airy, white-balance/exposure/colour correction, flat-lay/45-degree/side, close-but-needs-tweaking, ASAP), strengthened from a single-dish 3-frame recipe into an eight-frame matched set. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing (one upload, no folders, no repeated identical call): (a) cross-asset grade-MATCH of eight differently-lit frames to a single measurable house target — a common white point read off each frame's in-frame grey card by eye and a common lifted airy shadow floor — which forces NON-identical per-frame corrections (warm tungsten frames cooled and lifted, cool daylight frames warmed and pulled down, each by its own amount), authored from image_apply_adjustments primitives rather than a preset or an auto button; (b) an agent-AUTHORED signature look built from a MASKED primitive — a select_by_prompt food mask driving a bounded, no-rotation image_adjust_hsl saturation/luminance lift on the food that must pop the dish WITHOUT lifting or garishing the airy surround the house look depends on; (c) an honest two-stage gen-free reframe of the 3:2 hero to a 16:9 with headline negative space that also crops the reference card out; and (d) an applied-parameter report making 'matched' checkable. Every step is headless-confirmed [C], server=adobe: no [W] Express widget, no [A] async media, no [T] template. No banned capability: no generative expand/outpaint, no gen-fill, no upscale/super-resolution (all outputs downscale from ~3200-4000px camera-scale sources), no text-to-image, no object-removal-with-reconstruction, no background replacement, no compositing, no image_fill_area, no whole-image color_overlay sold as a masked edit, no auto_tone on the correct path, no render_*/merge layout authoring.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the acceptance artifact is a single matched bright-and-airy set — every frame's neutral grey card must resolve to ONE common house white point and the shadows to ONE common airy floor (open but not washed to white, never crushed to zero, no channel clipped), and the agent returns a parameter sheet listing per-frame temperature/tint/exposure/shadow plus the shared target. This is tripable by a craft decision: a set each 'auto-fixed' or run with one global set of sliders will diverge at the grey cards and be rejected, and identical reported numbers across the differently-lit frames are a visible fail. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight frames shot under two opposite casts, demanding the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections judged from each frame's own card and histogram, not one recipe; (2) an authored masked-HSL food pop that must enrich the dish while preserving the airy pastel surround, which forces the constraint-reasoning that image_adjust_hsl accepts a mask but image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image and a global vibrance push would garish the backdrop; plus an honest off-centre reframe that leaves headline negative space and removes the reference card. TRAP: the naive path — run an auto button or one stock bright preset on each of the eight and call it a matched set — looks right because every frame reads fine alone, but the auto keys off each frame's own histogram, so the cool daylight dishes stay cooler and brighter than the warm tungsten frames, the grey cards do not agree, and the set fails the one-white-point gate; a second trap is copying the hero's exact temp/exposure onto the opposite-cast frames; a third is popping the food with a whole-image saturation/vibrance push (or image_apply_color_overlay) that also saturates the airy surround and kills the high-key look instead of a masked HSL move; a fourth is cropping the reference card out BEFORE neutralising, destroying the white-balance reference. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side; the agent never reads a pixel): grey card neutral (R approx G approx B) at the common white point on all eight card-bearing masters, shadows lifted to the shared airy floor with no channel crushed to 0 or clipped to 255, hero straightened and reframed to 16:9 ~2880x1620 with one-sided negative space and the card removed, social teaser exactly 1080x1350, tiles ~1200x1200 with the card removed, and the returned per-frame parameter sheet showing non-identical corrections converging on the stated common target; neutrality is graded on the retained card-bearing graded masters, card-absence is checked separately on the delivered crops.
